evidence.excerpt: Celonis, August 2023 (Business Wire, via StreetInsider/ERP Today): Carsten Thoma appointed President, responsible for corporate strategy and development, marketing, platform ecosystem, culture and Celonis Labs, working alongside co-CEOs Alex Rinke and Bastian Nominacher; still President as of 2026.

Celonis, 12 May 2026 (company release, Business Wire): launch of the Celonis Context Model, a dynamic real-time digital twin of operations built on process data, and a definitive agreement to acquire Ikigai Labs (AI decision intelligence: planning, simulation, forecasting). Celonis gains exclusive rights to MIT patents Ikigai licensed; MIT becomes a Celonis shareholder; co-founder Devavrat Shah (MIT EECS) becomes Chief Scientist, Enterprise AI. Confirmed by Forrester, Constellation Research, diginomica, ERP Today.
Celonis, June 2021: $1 billion Series D at an $11 billion valuation (Bloomberg, Crunchbase News).

Celonis, August 2022 (PR Newswire, The SaaS News): $400 million Series D extension led by Qatar Investment Authority plus a $600 million credit facility, at a post-money valuation of nearly $13 billion. Tracxn: about $2.4 billion raised over 13 rounds; no priced equity round since 2022.

Celonis leadership per company releases and Craft/Comparably listings: Alexander Rinke and Bastian Nominacher, co-founders and co-CEOs; Carsten Thoma, President (marketing in his remit); Benoit Fouilland, CFO effective 1 Dec 2024 (ex-Contentsquare); Dilipkumar Khandelwal, Chief Customer Officer. Dave Peterson was CMO 2021-2023; no current CMO appears on any listing reached (celonis.com leadership page egress-blocked).
Celonis About page (via Tracxn/PitchBook summaries): founded 2011 in Munich; dual headquarters in Munich, Germany and New York, US.

MHP (a Porsche company) success story and Porsche AG's own Medium post: Porsche relies on Celonis for process mining; MHP has supported Porsche across more than 25 process-mining projects end to end, from inbound supplier processes to the production line, finance and supply chain; a Porsche process-mining centre of excellence works with Celonis and MHP.

fiaformulae.com: Porsche Motorsport will field two teams under its own marque from Season 13 (2026/27), the first GEN4 season, alongside a customer team (Cupra Kiro continues as a Porsche customer team in 2026/27), so three teams run the Porsche 99X Electric package; Porsche has committed to GEN4.

Porsche Motorsport (2025): the factory team races as the Porsche Formula E Team with TDK as official technology partner; TAG Heuer remains a Global Partner of Porsche Motorsport; other partners listed include Mobil 1, Loctite, Puma, NetApp, Cato Networks and Synopsys. None is a process-intelligence or operations-software company. Reported from the team's own page; the sponsor table carries only Porsche, TAG Heuer and Hugo Boss for this team.

Sponsor table (spec/active_sponsor_db.md §2, data/teams.json): Jaguar TCS Racing — TCS title (IT services), Castrol; Mahindra Racing — Tech Mahindra (software/tech integrator); Envision Racing — Sand Technologies (AI), Genpact (unverified); Andretti Formula E — TWG AI (Official AI Partner), Quest Global; Porsche Formula E Team — Porsche (parent), TAG Heuer and Hugo Boss (unverified legacy). No process-mining or operations-software brand on any Formula E roster.

Formula E calendar table: Season 12 closes with the London E-Prix double-header on 15-16 August 2026 (ten weeks from 8 June); Berlin E-Prix double-header at Tempelhof in Season 12 and again in Season 13; Season 13, the first GEN4 season, opens in Jeddah in December 2026.

brief.hq: Munich and New York (dual headquarters; founded 2011)
brief.deck: Celonis, the Munich- and New York-based process-intelligence company last valued at about $13B, launched the Celonis Context Model on 12 May 2026 and agreed to acquire MIT-linked Ikigai Labs, repositioning a platform Porsche already runs in production as the context layer for enterprise AI.
brief.the_case_p1: On 12 May 2026 Celonis launched the Celonis Context Model, a real-time digital twin of a company's operations built from process data, and signed a definitive agreement to acquire Ikigai Labs, whose forecasting and simulation software rests on patents licensed from MIT; MIT becomes a Celonis shareholder and Ikigai co-founder Devavrat Shah joins as Chief Scientist, Enterprise AI. Celonis last priced at about $13B in an August 2022 extension led by Qatar Investment Authority, after a $1B Series D at $11B in June 2021; it has raised roughly $2.4B in total. Revenue is not disclosed.
brief.the_case_p2: Formula E's technology lanes are held by integrators, not software: TCS titles the Jaguar, Tech Mahindra sits on the Mahindra, Sand Technologies on the Envision and TWG AI on the Andretti. No process-intelligence or operations-software brand is on the grid. Porsche AG already runs Celonis across supply chain and production, and Porsche is doubling its Formula E presence to two works teams for the first GEN4 season.
brief.why_now_callout: <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9'>WHY NOW</font>  The Context Model launched on 12 May and the Ikigai deal is closing; the marketing push runs through the autumn. Season 12 ends with the London double-header on 15-16 August, and Season 13 opens the GEN4 era with two Porsche entries, so the partner slate for the new cars is set this summer.
brief.why_team_para: Porsche runs Celonis inside its own operations: with MHP, its consulting subsidiary, it has used Celonis process mining across more than 25 projects from inbound supply chain to production and finance. The Formula E team is the sharpest public expression of that culture, and from Season 13 it doubles to two works entries that need partners. Its Season 12 roster is reported to include TDK, NetApp, Synopsys and Cato Networks; none is an operations-software brand.

brief.opening_angle_intro: Lead with Porsche's own Celonis deployment.
brief.opening_angle_quote: “Carsten, Porsche already runs Celonis from inbound logistics to the production line, and from Season 13 it fields two Formula E teams with no operations-software name on the cars. The London finale is ten weeks out. 25 minutes to talk about the second car?”
score_cells: Launch 12 May; GEN4 roster set over summer.
German enterprise AI; Porsche customer already.
Product launch needs amplifier; no deadline.
risks: The $13B mark is four years old and revenue is undisclosed; appetite for a first motorsport budget is unproven.
Lead with the Ikigai launch budget and a services-heavy structure; confirm the marketing envelope on the first call.
Porsche buys Celonis software; turning a supplier into a paying partner inverts the relationship.
Position it as a joint showcase of Porsche's own process programme, co-funded, with Celosphere as the stage.
brief.bottom_line: A product launch and an MIT-linked acquisition at a company last valued at $13B, a customer in Porsche that already runs the software, and a Formula E grid with no operations-software brand make Celonis the right name for Porsche's expanded GEN4 programme. What holds it back: no fresh capital since 2022 and no public revenue.

why_now.label: Trigger
why_now.text: On 12 May 2026 Celonis launched the Celonis Context Model, a real-time digital twin of a company's operations built from process data, and signed a definitive agreement to acquire Ikigai Labs, an AI decision-intelligence company whose planning, simulation and forecasting software rests on patents licensed from MIT. MIT becomes a Celonis shareholder and Ikigai co-founder Devavrat Shah, an MIT professor, joins as Chief Scientist, Enterprise AI.

why_now.label: A repositioning that needs a stage
why_now.text: The launch recasts Celonis from process-mining vendor to the context layer beneath enterprise AI agents, a message aimed at chief executives and boards rather than process engineers. Product repositioning of that kind is exactly what a motorsport platform amplifies: a live operations twin at a race team is the demonstration the pitch needs.

why_now.label: Capital position, honestly
why_now.text: Celonis last priced at about $13B in an August 2022 extension led by Qatar Investment Authority, after a $1B Series D at $11B in June 2021; it has raised roughly $2.4B in total and does not disclose revenue. There has been no new priced equity since 2022, which is why the score stops at 73 and why the deal is sized modestly and paid partly in software.

why_now.label: Calendar window
why_now.text: Season 12 closes with the London E-Prix double-header on 15-16 August, ten weeks from the row date. Season 13, the first GEN4 season, opens in Jeddah in December with Porsche running two works entries for the first time, so partner decisions for the new cars are being made over the summer.

why_team.label: Porsche already runs the product
why_team.text: Porsche AG relies on Celonis for process mining and, with MHP, its own consulting subsidiary, has run more than 25 process-mining projects from inbound supplier logistics to the production line, finance and supply chain, coordinated by a Porsche centre of excellence. A team sponsorship extends a deployment the group already trusts into its most visible engineering programme.

why_team.label: Two cars, one open lane
why_team.text: From Season 13 Porsche fields two works teams under its own marque alongside a customer team, so its partner inventory doubles at the moment the GEN4 car debuts. The factory team's Season 12 roster is reported to include TDK, NetApp, Synopsys, Cato Networks, Mobil 1, Loctite and Puma; none is a process-intelligence or operations-software brand.

why_team.label: The rest of the grid is taken by integrators
why_team.text: TCS titles the Jaguar and owns its technology narrative, Tech Mahindra sits on the Mahindra, Sand Technologies on the Envision and TWG AI on the Andretti. Those lanes belong to services and AI integrators who resell or compete with Celonis; Porsche has no such conflict.

why_team.label: German company, German team, American market
why_team.text: Celonis is headquartered in Munich and New York; Porsche Motorsport in Weissach. A German enterprise-software brand on a German works team plays at home in Berlin and, through Formula E's Miami and Mexico City rounds, in front of the US customers the New York headquarters serves.

value.label: Operational workstream (Mode A)
value.text: Celonis maps the team's race operations end to end: freight and parts flow across a global season, garage build and tear-down, spares approvals, supplier lead times and homologation paperwork, with the Context Model as a live digital twin the operations director can query and Ikigai's forecasting flagging bottlenecks before a race weekend. Porsche AG's process-mining centre of excellence supplies the method and the people.

value.label: Commercial lift for the team
value.text: A partner that sells to chief operating officers, chief financial officers and chief information officers brings a guest list of enterprise buyers to Berlin, London and the US rounds, the audience Porsche's technology partners want in the garage.

value.label: Content and ecosystem
value.text: A race team's operations are a legible, dramatic process: the digital twin of a race weekend is a story for broadcast and for Celosphere, Celonis' annual customer conference, and a reference deployment for the automotive and logistics accounts Celonis sells to.

value.label: What the team gives back
value.text: Official Process Intelligence Partner designation, livery on both works cars, naming of the team's operations twin, hospitality at Berlin and London, driver and engineering access for Celonis' channels, and a joint case study with Porsche AG.

ruled_out.reason: TCS is title partner and owns the enterprise-technology narrative; a direct services-integrator conflict.
Tech Mahindra holds the software and integration lane.
Sand Technologies (AI) and Genpact (services, unverified for Season 12) crowd the lane.
TWG AI is primary partner and Official AI Partner; Quest Global covers engineering services.

extended.ask: A 25-minute call with Carsten Thoma before the London finale to confirm the marketing envelope behind the Context Model launch, agree a Season 13 announcement window with Porsche Motorsport, and size an Official Process Intelligence Partner entry across both Porsche works cars.

# Celonis → Porsche Formula E Team — verification log (N° 200, 8 Jun 2026)

Built in-session at no API cost (no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in the sandbox) with Claude acting as
scanner, verifier and writer through the pipeline's injectable stages; the calendar table, sponsor
table, 13-rule audit and the 2-page render ran as code. The case sits on the row's date, 8 Jun 2026,
in rebuild mode; `celonis.run.json` is the case record `python -m intel.backfill --cases` imports.

**Sandbox limitation, stated plainly:** direct fetches of celonis.com, businesswire.com, prnewswire.com
and porsche.com were blocked by the egress proxy. Each claim below was checked against the search
summary of the primary page named as the evidence URL. Treat every VERIFIED line as REPORTED until a
person opens the link. Confidence is MEDIUM and the footer reads VERIFY BEFORE CIRCULATION.

## The trigger

Celonis' own release of 12 May 2026 (Business Wire): launch of the Celonis Context Model and a
definitive agreement to acquire Ikigai Labs; MIT becomes a shareholder; Devavrat Shah becomes Chief
Scientist, Enterprise AI. Confirmed by Forrester, Constellation Research, diginomica and ERP Today. The
row date is 8 Jun; the trigger is 27 days earlier, inside the 90-day window. It is a product-launch
and M&A trigger, not a capital event: the timing label is WARM, not HOT.

## Team choice

The thin row suggested Jaguar TCS Racing. Ruled out: TCS is title partner and an IT-services
integrator that owns Jaguar's technology narrative (a channel conflict for Celonis). Porsche Formula E
Team chosen because Porsche AG already runs Celonis in production (MHP success story; Porsche AG's own
post), the lane is open on the sponsor table, and Porsche doubles to two works entries in Season 13
(fiaformulae.com). The team's Season 12 partners (TDK, NetApp, Synopsys, Cato Networks, Mobil 1,
Loctite, Puma) come from the team's own page and are NOT in the sponsor table, which carries only
Porsche, TAG Heuer and Hugo Boss for this team; the brief says "reported to include" and never writes
them as a Brand-at-Team sponsorship sentence. Operator: consider adding those rows to the seed.
